findings.quote: Writing the exponent with the wrong sign gives a range larger than the whole visible universe, 10¹⁰ m, which is not physically sensible for a short-range force.
findings.note: Two errors. First, writing the exponent of 10⁻¹⁶ with the wrong sign gives 10¹⁶ m, which is the printed option 1, not option 3; so this entry points at the wrong option. Second, 10¹⁰ m is not larger than the visible universe — it is about 0.07 of the Earth-Sun distance, while the observable universe is of the order 10²⁶ m.
findings.fix: Writing the exponent with the wrong sign gives 10¹⁶ m, a distance far larger than any nucleus, which cannot be the range of a short-range force — this entry should point at option 1.

notes: Solved independently: the weak nuclear force is the shortest-range of the four fundamental interactions, with the range quoted at this level as about 10⁻¹⁶ m, smaller than a nuclear radius. Option 4. Both step equations are true as written, including the classification of gravitational and electromagnetic as infinite-range. common_mistakes[0] (option 2, confusing the weak-force range with the 10⁻¹⁰ m size of an atom) is correct and correctly mapped.
